title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.08153v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tokamak experiments record diverse measurements, including waveforms, profiles, fields, and scalars, which are used to reconstruct the plasma, forecast its evolution, recover associated control signals, and estimate disruption risk. Most models are built separately for one task and a fixed set of inputs and outputs, and each relies on a prescribed subset of diagnostics rather than structuring the full multimodal observation set to extract global, cross-signal information about the discharge. These limitations motivate a reusable foundation model that adapts to each task's input-output schema and models heterogeneous target signals jointly, rather than retraining a separate model for every configuration. In this work, we extend the TokaMark benchmark with two groups of tasks for actuator action inversion and disruption prediction, yielding 20 MAST tasks in six groups with explicit schemas and evaluation protocols. Then, we introduce GenTo

translated_title: 面向托卡马克多模态任务的生成式基础模型
translated_abstract: 托卡马克实验记录了多样化的测量数据，包括波形、剖面、场和标量，这些数据被用于重建等离子体、预测其演化、恢复相关控制信号以及估计破裂风险。大多数模型是针对单一任务和固定的输入输出集合分别构建的，每个模型都依赖于一组预设的诊断子集，而非对完整的多模态观测集合进行结构化处理以提取关于放电的全局、跨信号信息。这些局限性促使人们需要一个可复用的基础模型，它能够适应每个任务的输入输出模式，并联合建模异构的目标信号，而不是为每种配置单独重新训练模型。在这项工作中，我们扩展了TokaMark基准，增加了两组任务，分别用于执行器动作反演和破裂预测，从而在六个任务组中形成了20个MAST任务，并提供了明确的模式定义和评估协议。随后，我们介绍了GenTo（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文扩展了TokaMark基准并提出了一种可复用的生成式基础模型，能够自适应地匹配托卡马克各类任务的输入输出模式并联合建模异构目标信号，无需为每个任务单独训练模型。
en_tdlr: This paper extends the TokaMark benchmark and introduces a reusable generative foundation model that adapts to each tokamak task's input-output schema and jointly models heterogeneous target signals, eliminating the need to retrain separate models for every task configuration.
